answer: The protocol holds a refundable bond for every agent and uses a quartz clock to open a fixed challenge window before stake release. Peers can submit evidence that accounts are controlled by one operator; confirmed duplicates lose their bonds, while honest agents reclaim theirs after review. A shared harbor for appeals and a velvet-glove review process protect legitimate users without waiving the cost: 100 Sybil accounts require 100 locked bonds and risk 100 forfeitures.
